cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Show Me the Score
cards.instruction: Find out how they measure success, what they stand to gain, and where you currently rank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I accept your verdict on my picnic, tell me how you're measuring success. I'll hear the criteria first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone having fun. It looked successful to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me what a successful picnic gets you, and where my organizing ranks against last year's. We'll put those beside 'fun.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I get the activities budget renewed. Yours cost less, but last year's attracted more people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You may score cost and attendance separately. Now tell me which one decides my ranking when you ask for that renewal; I want to know what my success is being used to prove.

reason: Address all three exact pursuits through A evaluation authority: metric, evaluator budget benefit and comparative cost/attendance rank. B4 competing measures cause A5 governing-weight inquiry.
